bio.en: Bob Moesta is co-creator of the Jobs-to-be-Done framework (with Clay Christensen) and author of Job Moves, focused on helping people find careers and jobs that truly fit them.
bio.zh: Bob Moesta 是与 Clay Christensen 共同创立“待办任务”（Jobs-to-be-Done）框架的人，也是《Job Moves》一书的作者，专注于帮助人们找到真正适合自己的职业与工作。

summary.en: Bob introduces his book Job Moves, built on interviewing over a thousand people who switched jobs and finding most ended up worse because they didn't know themselves well enough. He shares the tactic of taking a “jobcation” to reset between roles and distinguishes job features (salary, title) from job experiences that actually keep people engaged. The conversation reframes career transitions as progress moments and offers a practical lens for making better job changes.
summary.zh: Bob 介绍了他的新书《Job Moves》，基于对上千名跳槽者的访谈，发现大多数人因不够了解自己而跳到了更差的工作。他分享了在角色之间“放个职假”（jobcation）来重置状态的技巧，并区分了工作“特征”（薪资、头衔）与真正让人投入的“体验”。对话把职业转换重新框定为“进步时刻”，并提供了做出更好工作选择的实用视角。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You just wrote a new book called Job Moves that I have right here. What's the big idea behind this book?
turns.zh: 你刚写了一本新书，叫《跳槽指南》，我手头正好有这本书。这本书的核心理念是什么？

turns.speaker: Bob Moesta
turns.en: The moment you stop making progress in your career is the moment you start looking for another job. And so over the last 15 years we've interviewed over a thousand people. I've coached almost a thousand people because I think there's a billion people a year who switched jobs and ultimately most of them end up with a job that's worse than the one they were at, but they don't know how to find it. They don't know themselves well enough.
turns.zh: 当你在职业生涯中停滞不前时，就是你开始寻找新工作的时候。过去15年里，我们采访了超过1000人，我还指导了近千人。因为我发现每年有数十亿人换工作，但大多数人最终找到的工作比原来的更差，只不过他们不知道如何找到更好的机会。他们对自己不够了解。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's a very tactical piece of advice in your book, which is they do have a jobcation.
turns.zh: 书中有一个很实用的建议，叫“工作度假”。

turns.speaker: Bob Moesta
turns.en: When you're in a startup, it changes who you are and the moment that you get out of that environment, you need to take the time to reset your mind and your body. I call it a jobcation, which is a job I can go do with one hand tie by hide my back so I can rest and recover to go do something else. It's about actually being able to go to the gym and work out and have some vacations. The moment you are comfortable doing nothing, you know who you are again, and you can actually figure this out.
turns.zh: 在初创公司工作时，它会重塑你的个性。当你离开那个环境后，需要花时间调整身心状态。我把这叫做“工作度假”——就是能用一只手打理工作、隐藏后方、放松恢复，之后再去迎接新挑战。关键在于能去健身房锻炼、度假放松。当你能自在地休息时，你才能重新认识自己，找到方向。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You have this really interesting distinction in the book between job features like salary and title and job experiences.
turns.zh: 书中对薪资、职位等工作要素和工作体验做了很有趣的区分。

turns.speaker: Bob Moesta
turns.en: It's very simple, very similar to product. There's difference between product features and product experiences, and what you start to realize is it's the experiences that keep you at your job. It's not just about the money because you start to realize money is a surrogate for respect, or I've got bills to pay or I'm falling behind. Money has actually many, many different implications to it because everybody wants more money, but the question is why do you want more money?
turns.zh: 道理很简单，跟产品设计很像。产品有功能和体验之分，后来我意识到，正是工作体验让你留在岗位上。钱不是唯一因素，因为你会发现钱是尊重的替代品，或者是为了支付账单、避免落后。钱的意义远不止于此，每个人都想赚更多钱，但关键是为什么想赚更多？
